verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego', 'Orion will splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean off California, ... Pacific Ocean off the San Diego coast'; R3/R4/R5: similar mentions of Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast on April 10, 2026.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the splashdown location and date matching the claim exactly.

verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II crew splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and timezone conversion stated directly in multiple sources for April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded with the splashdown and was a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'complete a historic 10-day mission', 'traveled around the moon'; R3: 'ending the record-breaking 10-day mission'; R4: '10-day trip to the moon'; R1: mission from April 1 to April 10 splashdown, lunar flyby.
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as a 10-day mission concluding with splashdown and involving a lunar flyby/orbit; precise duration slightly under 10 full days but commonly referred to as 10-day.

verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and ... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen'; similar in R3/R4.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew returned in the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion will splash down'; R2: 'Orion will re-enter ... capsule'; R3/R4: 'Orion capsule' returns crew.
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state the crew returned via Orion capsule splashdown.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed deep-space return in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first humans toward the Moon since 1972', 'more than 50 years'; R2: 'first crewed flight beyond Earth orbit since Apollo'; R3: 'last time humans landed on the moon was in 1972'; R4: 'first time in over 53 years'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm first crewed lunar/deep-space mission/return since Apollo era, over 50 years prior to 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission goal is to verify the Orion spacecraft and SLS rocket systems for future lunar missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'ensure the Orion spacecraft and SLS rocket are ready for longer lunar missions'; R1: 'evaluated Orion’s systems ... SLS rocket'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in R2 matches exactly; R1 supports Orion/SLS evaluation for deep-space.

verifications.claim: A SpaceX Falcon 9 launch was scheduled for late Friday night (April 10, 2026) from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launch set for 7:39 PT same night' (April 10, 2026), in California sonic boom context.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SpaceX Falcon 9 launch scheduled evening of April 10, 2026 ('late Friday night'), in California, but do not specify Vandenberg Space Force Base.

verifications.claim: The SpaceX Falcon 9 launch was separate from the NASA Artemis II mission
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: '2 sonic booms possible ... Artemis II splashdown, SpaceX launch'; separate events same night.
verifications.reasoning: R5 explicitly presents SpaceX launch and Artemis II splashdown as distinct events causing separate sonic booms.
